channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Syrian Kurdish leader announces SDF dissolution after its integration into army
item.description: Mazloum Abdi, the commander-in-chief of the Syrian Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on Tuesday announced the dissolution of the group in a televised speech from the presidential palace in Damascus. The dissolution followed the integration of SDF fighters into the Syrian military, said Abdi, and represented a major victory for Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Beloved US country music icon Dolly Parton dies at 80
item.description: US singer-songwriter, actress, businesswoman and philanthropist Dolly Parton died on Tuesday at the age of 80, her family said in a statement. The prolific songwriter released 49 studio albums, more than 100 compilation and collorabative albums, won 10 Grammys and 13 Academy of Country Music awards, and racked up 26 number one country hits during her six decades in the American music scene.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Nigeria’s president orders rescue operation after mass kidnapping at mosque
item.description: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday ordered security agencies to conduct a rescue operation after the mass kidnapping of worshippers during an attack on a mosque in the north-central Niger State last week. Local authorities were still trying to verify the number of missing people, but local residents said roughly 600 women, children and elderly people had been abducted.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Japan: 1,800 people pull 360-tonne Hirosaki Castle keep by hand
item.description: About 1,800 people came together in northern Japan to pull a 360-tonne castle keep by hand. The Hirosaki Castle keep was moved in 2015 so its earthquake-damaged stone wall could undergo repairs. Now, using hikiya, a technique that places buildings on rollers so they can be moved without dismantling them, the keep is being brought closer to its original position. Those taking part were selected through a lottery system. Moving efforts will continue until the end of August.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Cyberattacks target French government agencies
item.description:
🇫🇷 🧑‍💻 French government agencies are more frequently landing in the crosshairs of hackers, leaving important personal data increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks.
In 2026 alone, organs of the French finance ministry have been victim to three massive cyberattacks, compromising the data of millions of people.
FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains what they have revealed - and why you should be concerned.
#France #data #cyberattack #finance
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Canada strikes back at Trump with retaliatory tariffs as US trade war escalates
item.description: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion ($19.94 billion) worth of US goods, including steel and dairy products, in a dollar-for-dollar response to President Donald Trump's punitive tariffs on Canadian products. Ottawa also announced a C$7.5 billion aid package for impacted Canadian businesses and workers as the trade war between the two countries escalated.
item.source: © Justin Tang, AP via The Canadian Press
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: French astronaut performs second spacewalk in just a week
item.description: One week after becoming the first French woman to perform a spacewalk, Sophie Adenot has ventured outside the International Space Station again on August 25 - with the mission of replacing an antenna.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Canada's tariffs on US about 'sovereignty to get people on board' with trade war
item.description: As its trade war with the US deepens, Canada is imposing tariffs on US goods in retaliation for tariffs introduced in the past few days on its goods. Ottawa has also announced a multi-billion aid package for workers and has called on Canadians to buy local to help domestic industries. FRANCE 24's Christopher Guly and Kethevane Gorjestani tell us what to know.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Iran offers $10 million to kill Trump's son
item.description: Iranian state media has aired a video that appears to threaten the life of Barron Trump, US President Donald Trump's youngest son. Since the start of the war in February, Iranian media have on multiple occasions circulated content threatening the president and family members. The US Secret Service has confirmed it is aware of the video.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Replay: Canada announces countermeasures to new US tariffs
item.description: Rewatch as Canadian ministers lay out a series of countermeasures as its trade war with the US deepens after the Trump administration imposed new tariffs on Canadian goods.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Tornado ravages small village
item.description: 🌪️ A tornado of rare intensity devastated the small village of Pomas in southern France, causing widespread destruction and leaving residents in shock on Tuesday, with the mayor describing the aftermath as resembling "wartime". At least 39 people were injured, including two severely.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: CIA director Ratcliffe visits Moscow, US media reports
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe ​visited Russia to attend meetings in Moscow on Tuesday, according to two US media outlets, in what is believed to be Ratcliffe's first known trip to Russia since taking over as US spy chief. The reported visit comes as US-brokered talks aimed at ending the Ukraine war have stalled.

item.title: Space: Second spacewalk for French astronaut Sophie Adenot
item.description: A week after her first historic spacewalk, French astronaut Sophie Adenot began her second spacewalk outside the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday as part of her mission. Here are some (time-lapsed) images from the start of the extravehicular activity, which aims to replace a communications antenna. The spacewalk is expected to last around six and a half hours.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Not an isolated incident’: Russian drones stalk Ukraine’s civilians in ‘human safaris’
item.description: The video of a Ukrainian cyclist being targeted and killed by a short-range drone posted – and later deleted – by the Russian military Friday left viewers outraged and shaken. But it’s not the first time that Russian drone operators have been accused of terrorising Ukrainian civilians by deliberately targeting them in “human safaris” denounced as a war crime by an independent UN commission.
item.dc:creator: Sébastian SEIBT

item.title: French village takes stock of tornado aftermath
item.description: Dozens of people were injured after a tornado ravaged a small village in southern France. According to local authorities in Pomas, two people are in critical condition. Over 1,400 homes are still without electricity on August 25.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Anger mounts in Haiti as new attack shows power held by gang coalition
item.description: At least 47 people were killed in a farming community near Port-au-Prince after the area was attacked by a gang coalition. For the gang, the goal is to get their hands on a highly strategic area near the Haitian capital. But how could they have led such a violent attack? FRANCE 24's Catherine Norris-Trent tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: What to know about French astronaut Sophie Adenot's second spacewalk
item.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot is exiting the International Space Station for the second time in just a week. The rare double occurrence is taking place as astronauts on the ISS are looking to finish repairs on their ship. FRANCE 24's James André tells us more on the repairs to be done and how to prepare for such a mission.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US economic D-Day sanctions: 'Repeated bombing attacks across Iran failed to change the calculus'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Imran Bayoumi, Deputy Director & Resident Fellow at the Atlantic Council. He sees the Trump administration’s new sanctions strategy toward Iran as an attempt to seek economic leverage where military force has so far failed to produce any results. But its effectiveness rests on several unresolved assumptions. Chief among them is whether Washington can compel China, Iran’s largest oil customer, to comply despite Beijing’s growing economic resilience. Iran, meanwhile, has decades of experience curtailing sanctions and is again threatening regional escalation.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: With sanctions and tariffs, US bets on its economic power to get what it wants
item.description: The US has announced a new wave of sanctions on Iran and has promised to sanction any countries trading with it - including China. It also comes as the US deepens a trade war with its neighbour Canada. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US removes Syria off its list of state sponsors of terrorism
item.description: Turkey has welcomed a US decision to remove Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism. The move rescinds a decades-old designation which came with severe economic consequences for Damascus. Corresponding sanctions relief for Syria have also been announced.
